tool.name: sourmash compare
tool.description: Build an N×N similarity matrix from a collection of signatures
tool.command: mkdir -p stage && ## Stage every signature in the list collection under a name keyed by its ## element_identifier, so the work dir is readable and the .sig files can be ## named on the command line individually. #for $sig in $signatures ln -s '$sig' 'stage/${sig.element_identifier}.sig' && #end for ## ⛔ NAMED EXPLICITLY, NOT `stage/*.sig`. sourmash's CSV columns follow the ## command line, and a glob is sorted by the SHELL -- so the matrix came out in ## filename order (and, since bash sorts pathname expansion by LC_COLLATE, in an ## order that depends on the job's locale). Every other WF-A output is in PANEL ## order: `signatures` is this collection mapped over, `sizes` comes off the ## assemblies, and `self_pairs`/`relabel_map` follow the element identifiers. The ## matrix was the one artifact that disagreed, including with the `signatures` ## collection published beside it out of this same workflow. ## ⚠ AND ONE WORKFLOW PUBLISHING TWO ORDERS IS NOT A COSMETIC PROBLEM HERE. In ## WF-C2, chains filtered out of WF-C arrived alphabetical against a panel-ordered ## grid and every projection took the wrong chain, with correct-looking ## identifiers throughout. This iterates the collection, so the order is the ## panel's and nothing about the shell can change it. sourmash compare --ksize $ksize -o cmp --csv '$output' #for $sig in $signatures 'stage/${sig.element_identifier}.sig' #end for && ## clustered heatmap + dendrogram (scipy hierarchical clustering; matplotlib in the env) sourmash plot --labels cmp #if str($containment) == "true" && ## ⛔ CONTAINMENT, BECAUSE JACCARD IS CONFOUNDED BY ASSEMBLY SIZE. Jaccard divides by the ## UNION, so a 286 Mb assembly caps at 286/800 = 0.36 against an 800 Mb genome EVEN AS A ## PERFECT SUBSET, and a 2,297 Mb unpurged one caps at ~0.35 against the same genome. Both ## tails read as distant for a reason that is not relatedness, and this matrix is what WF-I's ## fold order consumes. ## ⚠ OFF BY DEFAULT and emitted as a SECOND matrix, never in place of the first: the Jaccard ## output is what the heatmap and dendrogram are drawn from and what every downstream consumer ## already reads. ## ⚠ AND NOTHING IS PLOTTED FROM IT -- containment(A,B) != containment(B,A) whenever the two ## differ in size, so a dendrogram drawn from it would be an artefact of the clustering, not a ## relationship. ## Same explicit-argument ordering as above, for the same reason: the CSV columns follow the ## command line, and a shell glob would order them by locale instead of by panel. sourmash compare --ksize $ksize --containment --csv '$containment_matrix' #for $sig in $signatures 'stage/${sig.element_identifier}.sig' #end for && ## ⚠ THE SYMMETRIC ONE, AND THE ONLY SIZE-ROBUST MATRIX THAT CAN BE A TREE. Plain containment is ## asymmetric, so clustering it yields an artefact of whichever triangle the algorithm read; ## max(containment(A,B), containment(B,A)) is symmetric and still never divides by the union. ## Its heatmap and dendrogram sit beside the Jaccard pair rather than replacing them -- where the ## two trees disagree, the Jaccard one is the one distorted by size. sourmash compare --ksize $ksize --max-containment -o maxc --csv '$max_containment_matrix' #for $sig in $signatures 'stage/${sig.element_identifier}.sig' #end for && sourmash plot --labels maxc #end if

param.name: signatures
param.label: Signature list collection
param.help: A 'list' collection of sourmash signature files (e.g. from sourmash sketch, mapped over strains). The element identifier of each element should be the strain name; it is staged as '{strain}.sig'. The signature names become the matrix row/column labels.

param.name: containment
param.label: Also emit a containment matrix
param.help: Asymmetric, and robust to assembly size: |A n B| / |A|. Jaccard divides by the union, so on a panel spanning 286 Mb to 2,297 Mb it penalises a size difference as if it were distance. Off by default because it adds an output and this workflow's output set is consumed downstream.

param.label: k-mer size
param.help: k-mer size to select from each signature for the comparison (default 31). Must match a k-mer size present in the sketched signatures.

tool.help:
**sourmash compare** — compute an N×N similarity matrix from a set of MinHash signatures.
Given a collection of sourmash signatures (one per strain/genome, typically produced by ``sourmash sketch`` mapped over a list of strains), this tool runs ``sourmash compare`` to estimate the Jaccard similarity between every pair of signatures and writes the resulting symmetric N×N matrix as CSV.
-----
**Input**
- *Signature list collection* — a ``list`` collection of sourmash signature files. Each element's identifier should be the strain name; elements are staged as ``{strain}.sig`` and then named individually on the command line, **in collection order**, so the matrix column order is the panel's -- not the shell's. (A `stage/*.sig` glob sorted by filename, and by the job's ``LC_COLLATE`` at that.) The matrix row/column **labels** are the signature ``name`` fields, which normally match the strain names.
**Output**
- ``compare.csv`` — an N×N similarity matrix (datatype ``csv``). The first row is the header of strain labels; each subsequent row is one strain's similarities to every strain, with ``1.0`` self-similarity on the diagonal.
-----
**Key options**
- ``--ksize`` k-mer size to select from each signature (default 31). It must match a k-mer size present in the sketched signatures.
-----
**Implementation note**
The wrapper symlinks every element of the list collection into a staging directory as ``{element_identifier}.sig`` and invokes ``sourmash compare`` with those paths listed explicitly, in collection order.
